name: Miacademy
benefit: math that adapts at every answer
line: Miacademy covers every subject at a grade the parent picks. AMP is only math, set by the learner's answers.
description: AMP vs Miacademy: an all-subject K-8 homeschool program with parent-set grades, beside a math-only program that sets each problem from the last answer.
verdict: Miacademy covers every subject from kindergarten to grade 8 in one subscription, with video lessons, games, a gradebook and accreditation as a supplementary program, for $480 a year per student [1][5][8]. Its math follows a grade level the parent chooses [5][6]. AMP is only math: it finds the level in each strand from the answers, explains every miss, and brings old skills back on a schedule, from counting through precalculus.

reasons.title: The level comes from answers, not a grade pick
reasons.body: In Miacademy the parent chooses the grade level that fits the child, and a learner can skip known topics or switch levels [5][6][7]. We found no placement test or adaptive engine described on its math pages [2][5][6][7]. AMP finds the level in each of 14 strands of math within the first 24 problems, then chooses every next problem from the answers: new work, a prerequisite, or review. A learner at grade 3 in fractions and grade 6 in geometry gets practice at both.

reasons.title: Every answer is checked and explained
reasons.body: Miacademy's math pages describe video lessons, then practice questions, extension activities and review games [5][6]. We found no description of what a learner sees after a wrong answer. In AMP every answer shows right or wrong, the correct answer and the worked steps. In a review of 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.05 for marking right or wrong alone. These are averages by feedback type, not a head-to-head trial [12].

reasons.title: Help is never counted as mastery
reasons.body: AMP calls a skill Strong when four of the last five answers are right without help. Its hint gives the first step, never the answer, and an answer given after a hint or the lesson does not count. Two misses in a row send practice back to what the skill builds on. We found no mastery rule on Miacademy's math pages [5][6][7]. On MiaPrep, the parent sets the passing grade [4].

reasons.title: Old skills come back on a timed schedule
reasons.body: Miacademy's kindergarten math follows a spiral that revisits skills [7]. We found no schedule for when a skill returns. AMP brings each learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics, and a miss starts the schedule over. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed, spaced practice scored 61% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [11].

reasons.title: Only math, from counting through precalculus
reasons.body: Miacademy spreads one subscription across math, reading, science, social studies, electives and world languages [1]. Its math runs from counting to algebra and geometry for kindergarten through grade 8 [2]. MiaPrep continues to grade 12, but its page names no math courses [1][4]. AMP is only math, on one map of 336 skills through precalculus, and it fits beside any homeschool plan, including one that keeps Miacademy for the other subjects.

reasons.title: Workbooks printed for this learner, with answer keys
reasons.body: Miacademy offers printable PDF extension activities, and full-course workbooks for some courses in its store [7]. We found nothing saying they are made for the individual learner. AMP prints unlimited workbooks built from each learner's own record, each with a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level.

rows.price: $48 a month after a $1.99 first month, or $480 a year, per student, every subject. Lifetime: $1,120, or $2,520 for up to four students [1].
rows.buyers: Families, directly [1]. It lists funding programs in 26 states, some closed, paused or not usable for homeschooling [3].
rows.range: Math from counting to algebra and geometry, kindergarten through grade 8 [2]. MiaPrep covers grades 7 to 12; its page names no math courses [1][4].
rows.start: The parent chooses a grade level. We found no placement test on its math pages [5][6][7].
rows.teaching: Video lessons with demonstrations, then practice questions, extension activities and review games [5][6].
rows.next: A fixed course sequence. The parent can customize units and lessons; a learner can skip known topics or switch grades [5][6][7].
rows.mastery: No mastery rule found on its math pages [5][6][7]. On MiaPrep, the parent sets the passing grade [4].
rows.review: A spiral that revisits skills, per its kindergarten math page [7]. No review schedule found.
rows.print: Printable PDF extension activities. Full-course workbooks for some courses, sold in its store [7].
rows.adult: Chooses the grade level, can customize units and lessons, and keeps the gradebook [1][5][6].
rows.reports: A built-in gradebook with downloadable grade and attendance reports [1].
rows.evidence: No outcome study on its site. No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026 [8][9][10].

theirs: Miacademy is an online homeschool program from Miaplaza Inc. It calls itself "a full K–8 homeschool curriculum" and covers math, reading, science, social studies, electives and world languages in one subscription [1]. The company reports more than 100,000 families, more than 3,000 lessons and over 80 courses. Its sister program, MiaPrep, continues through grades 7 to 12 [1].

In math, a learner watches video lessons with demonstrations, then works practice questions, extension activities and review games [5][6]. The kindergarten course follows a spiral that revisits skills [7]. The parent chooses a grade level and can change the plan unit by unit and lesson by lesson. A learner can skip known topics or switch levels without repeating [5][6][7].

Learners earn Gold for completed work and spend it in a Design Studio on shop products, pets and review games [5][6]. Miacademy offers text-to-speech, untimed tests and a built-in gradebook with grade and attendance reports [1]. ACS-WASC accredits it as a supplementary education program [8].
credit: Every subject from kindergarten to grade 8 in one subscription, at $480 a year per student, less than AMP's $599 a year for the first child, for math alone [1]. Lifetime plans as well.
Text-to-speech and untimed tests [1]. AMP does not read problems aloud.
Review games and a reward economy: learners earn Gold and spend it on shop products and pets [5][6]. AMP has no games or rewards store.
Accreditation from ACS-WASC as a supplementary program, a gradebook with attendance reports, and listed funding programs in 26 states [1][3][8]. AMP is not accredited and takes three state funds.

theirs: We found no study of how much students learn with Miacademy. Its accreditation page lists awards and testimonials and makes no claim of studies, test scores or measured outcomes, and its homepage and curriculum page link to no research page [1][2][8]. Miacademy has no entry in Evidence for ESSA, and the What Works Clearinghouse has no intervention report on it (checked November 2026) [9][10].

Its public numbers describe reach: more than 100,000 families, more than 3,000 lessons and over 80 courses [1]. Its accreditation comes from ACS-WASC, as a supplementary education program [8]. In our view, neither a family count nor accreditation tells how much students learn.
ours: We built AMP on findings from trials and reviews. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, against 0.05 for marking right or wrong alone. These are averages by feedback type, and effects were smaller in primary and high school settings [12]. Mixed, spaced practice scored 61% against 38% for practice in blocks a month later, in a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations. The test was the researchers' own, and the mixed practice was also spaced [11]. Miacademy's spiral shares the idea of returning to old skills [7]; AMP times each return to the learner's own answers. We expect that to show in outcomes, and we have committed in public to measuring it.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each is registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want one subscription for every subject, not math alone.
Your child needs problems read aloud, or wants games and rewards along the way.
You want an accredited supplementary program with a gradebook and attendance records.
You want a one-time lifetime price, or your state's education fund lists Miacademy and not AMP.
amp: Math is the subject you most want done right, at your child's level in every part of it.
You want each next problem chosen from the last answer, and every miss explained with worked steps.
You want old skills to come back on a schedule, without planning it.
Your learner is past grade 8, or headed for algebra, geometry and precalculus.
You like Miacademy for other subjects and want a separate math program beside it.

questions.question: Is AMP more expensive than Miacademy?
questions.answer: Yes. Miacademy costs $480 a year or $48 a month per student, for every subject, and lists discounts and payment plans [1][13]. AMP costs $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child and $399 or $39 for each more, for math alone. For that, AMP finds the level in every strand, chooses every problem, schedules review and prints workbooks from counting through precalculus.

questions.question: Does Miacademy adapt to my child?
questions.answer: The parent chooses a grade level, and a learner can skip known topics or switch levels [5][6][7]. We found no placement test or adaptive engine described on Miacademy's math pages [6]. MiaPrep says its learning path is adjusted daily based on student progress, without saying how [4].

questions.question: Can we use AMP and Miacademy together?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is only math, so it can take over math while Miacademy covers the other subjects. The first 100 answers and 5 workbooks for each learner are free, with no card.

questions.question: Does Miacademy teach high school math?
questions.answer: Miacademy's math runs through grade 8 [2]. MiaPrep continues to grade 12, but its page names no math courses [4]. AMP runs through Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Precalculus.
